# FuelPilot

> FuelPilot is a turn-by-turn navigation app for iPhone and Android that plans your fuel stops. It knows your tank size, learns your real MPG from your fill-ups and checks fuel prices along your whole route, then picks the cheapest stations you can reach before you run low. Every trip you navigate is logged with its miles and fuel for taxes and IFTA. It works in the United States and Canada.

Key facts:

- Who it's for: drivers of diesel pickups, RVs and motorhomes, anyone towing a trailer, hot shot and semi drivers, and people who log miles for work.
- Platforms: iPhone (App Store, https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823442691) and Android (Google Play, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ghostsystems.fuelpilot). Big Rig is on iPhone now and comes to Android in the next update.
- Price: free to download and use. FuelPilot Pro is $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year. FuelPilot Big Rig is $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year and includes everything in Pro. Both start with a 7-day free trial. US prices.
- Free: turn-by-turn navigation with spoken directions, the cheapest gas near you, fuel prices along your route (with a free account), a 7-day trip logbook, one vehicle.
- Pro: Fuel Autopilot (plans and adds every fuel stop for the trip at the cheapest station you can reach, then re-checks after each fill-up), receipt photo reading, the full logbook, mileage log / fuel expense / quarterly IFTA exports as spreadsheets, more than one vehicle, towing mode.
- Big Rig: truck-legal routes for the rig's height, weight and length (plus axles, trailers and hazmat), avoiding low bridges, weight limits and restricted roads; for semis and hot shots, fuel stops at truck stops and truck lanes only, at the truck-lane diesel price; RV routing that clears the motorhome's size; a road-ahead list of upcoming fuel stops, truck stops, weigh stations, rest areas, restrictions, and weather and road alerts (weigh station locations, not open/closed status). Can be switched off to drive a car.
- No OBD-II adapter needed: it plans from tank size, the fuel level you set and the MPG it learns.
- Fuel discounts and memberships: enter discounts once; Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's and cardlock stations only show if you have a membership.
- Fuel prices come from HERE Technologies.
- Not yet available: Apple CarPlay (built, turned on in a later update). No Android Auto.
- Made by Ghost Systems LLC, a small US company founded by David Kulagin, a diesel mechanic who hauls for work.
- Compared with GasBuddy: GasBuddy is best known for user-reported gas prices, the GasBuddy card and a trip cost calculator; FuelPilot is a navigation app that plans stops from your tank and range, adds them to your route and logs the trip.
- Compared with Trucker Path: Trucker Path is made for semi drivers, with parking availability, weigh station status and a large trucker community; its Diamond plan ($29.99 a month or $249.99 a year) includes fuel plans. FuelPilot Big Rig ($19.99 a month or $199.99 a year) is built around fuel planning and trip records, including IFTA miles by state, and works for cars, pickups and RVs as well as trucks.

## Home page (https://fuelpilotapp.com/)

### What is FuelPilot?
FuelPilot is a turn-by-turn navigation app for iPhone and Android that plans your fuel stops. It knows your tank size, learns your real MPG from your fill-ups and checks fuel prices along your whole route, then picks the cheapest stations you can reach before you run low. Every trip you navigate is logged with its miles and fuel, ready for taxes and IFTA.
- Who it's for
  Drivers of diesel pickups, RVs and motorhomes, anyone towing a trailer, hot shot and semi drivers, and people who log miles for work
- Phones
  iPhone on the App Store and Android on Google Play
- Where it works
  United States and Canada
- Price
  Free to use. Pro is $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year. Big Rig is $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year. Both start with a 7-day free trial.
- Fuel prices
  From HERE Technologies, refreshed regularly
- Made by
  Ghost Systems LLC, a small US company started by a diesel mechanic who hauls for work
- Towing a trailer or driving an RV
- Driving a semi or hot shot
- Logging miles for work
### How a drive works
- 1 Pick a destination Search for a place or drop a pin, then choose between routes. You get turn-by-turn directions with spoken guidance.
- 2 FuelPilot knows your range It knows your tank size and learns your real MPG from your fill-ups, so it always knows how far you can go.
- 3 It plans every fuel stop Before you leave, Autopilot picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the whole trip. After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense.
- 4 The trip logs itself Miles, time, fuel and stops go into your logbook, ready for your records or your accountant.
### What's in the app
Navigation, fuel prices and your trip records in one place. Features marked Pro come with FuelPilot Pro. Big Rig mode comes with FuelPilot Big Rig.
#### Fuel Autopilot Pro
Every fuel stop for the trip, planned up front from prices along your whole route. You choose your reserve, how far out of the way you'll go and how much a detour has to save.
#### Turn-by-turn navigation
Spoken directions, rerouting and weather on the map. Avoid tolls or highways, and find a restroom, food, a rest area or a truck stop in one tap.
#### Cheapest gas near you
Tap Get gas to find the lowest price within the distance you set, from 1 to 20 miles.
#### The price you actually pay
Enter your fuel discounts once and every pick plans on your price. Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's and cardlock stations only show up if you have a membership.
#### Learns your real MPG
FuelPilot works out your real MPG from the gallons you put in and the miles you drove, so your range keeps getting more accurate. Nothing to plug in.
#### A logbook that writes itself
Every navigated drive is saved with its route map, miles, time, MPG, stops and what you saved on fuel. Tag trips business or personal and add notes.
#### Receipts read for you Pro
Take a photo of the receipt and the station, gallons, price and total fill themselves in. Prefer to type them? Turn photo reading off in Settings.
#### Ready for tax time Pro
Export a mileage log, a fuel expense report or a quarterly IFTA summary with miles and gallons by state, as a spreadsheet file.
#### Every vehicle, towing included Pro
Each vehicle keeps its own tank size and MPG, and towing mode adjusts your range when there's a trailer behind you.
#### Big Rig mode Big Rig
For semis, hot shots and RVs. Enter your rig's height, weight and length and FuelPilot plans truck-legal routes around low bridges, weight limits and restricted roads, and only sends you to truck stops and truck lanes. The road-ahead list shows your fuel stops, truck stops, weigh stations, rest areas and weather and road alerts coming up. Switch it off any time to drive a car.
### Free, Pro and Big Rig
Navigation and nearby prices are free. Pro adds the parts that save money and paperwork on every trip. Big Rig adds truck routing for semis, hot shots and RVs.

### Questions
More answers on the support page.
#### Is there an app that plans fuel stops for a whole road trip?
Yes. FuelPilot's Autopilot plans every fuel stop for the trip before you leave. It picks the cheapest stations you can reach with your reserve left, on or close to your route, and adds them to your directions. After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense. Autopilot comes with FuelPilot Pro. With a free account you still see fuel prices along your route.
#### What's a good app for planning fuel stops when towing a trailer?
FuelPilot is built for it. Towing cuts your MPG and your range, so with towing mode on FuelPilot adjusts your range for the trailer and plans stops you can actually reach. You choose how much fuel to keep in reserve and how far out of the way you'll go for a cheaper price. Towing mode comes with Pro. See FuelPilot for towing and RVs.
#### Does FuelPilot do truck routing for semis, hot shots and RVs?
Yes, with FuelPilot Big Rig. Enter your rig's height, weight and length and it plans truck-legal routes around low bridges, weight limits and restricted roads. For a semi or hot shot it only sends you to truck stops and truck lanes, at the truck-lane diesel price. Truck routes depend on map data and the sizes you enter, so always follow posted signs and use your own judgment. Big Rig is on iPhone now and comes to Android in the next update. See FuelPilot for truckers.
#### How is FuelPilot different from GasBuddy?
GasBuddy is best known for gas prices reported by its users, the GasBuddy card discount and a trip cost calculator. FuelPilot is a navigation app: it gives you turn-by-turn directions, plans where to stop based on your tank and range, adds those stops to your route and logs the trip. Many drivers use a price app and a maps app together. FuelPilot puts both jobs in one. See FuelPilot vs GasBuddy.
#### How is FuelPilot different from Trucker Path?
Trucker Path is made for semi drivers, with truck stop parking availability, weigh station status and a large trucker community. FuelPilot is built around fuel planning and trip records, and works for cars, pickups and RVs as well as trucks. With Big Rig you can switch truck routing off and drive your personal vehicle in the same app. See Trucker Path alternatives.
#### Can FuelPilot track my mileage for taxes or IFTA?
Yes. Every drive you navigate with FuelPilot is saved to your logbook with its route, miles, time and fuel, and you can tag trips business or personal. With Pro you can export a mileage log, a fuel expense report or a quarterly IFTA summary with miles and gallons by state, as a spreadsheet. Drives you don't navigate with FuelPilot aren't logged. See FuelPilot as a mileage log.
#### Is FuelPilot free?
Yes. Navigation, the cheapest gas near you and a 7-day trip logbook are free, and a free account adds fuel prices along your route. Pro ($7.99 a month or $49.99 a year) adds Autopilot fuel stops, receipt reading, the full logbook with exports, and more than one vehicle with towing mode. Big Rig ($19.99 a month or $199.99 a year) adds truck routing. Both start with a 7-day free trial.
#### Do I need an OBD-II adapter or anything plugged in?
No. FuelPilot plans from your tank size, the fuel level you set and the MPG it learns from your fill-ups.
#### Does FuelPilot work in Canada?
Yes. FuelPilot works in the United States and Canada.
#### Does FuelPilot work with Apple CarPlay or Android Auto?
Not yet. CarPlay is built and will be turned on in a later update.

## Towing and RVs (https://fuelpilotapp.com/towing/)

### Fuel stop planning for towing and RVs
A trailer can cut your MPG by a third or more, so the range you're used to is wrong the moment you hitch up. FuelPilot plans your fuel stops around the range you really have while towing, picks the cheapest station you can reach, and gives you turn-by-turn directions there.
### How it works when you tow
- Towing mode adjusts your range. Each vehicle keeps its own tank size and MPG, and with towing mode on FuelPilot adjusts your range for the trailer behind you.
- It learns your real MPG. FuelPilot works out your MPG from the gallons you put in and the miles you drove, so your range gets more accurate with every fill-up. Nothing to plug in.
- Autopilot plans every stop. Before you leave, it picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the whole trip, keeping the reserve you choose. After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense.
- You set the rules. Choose how much fuel to keep in reserve, how far out of the way you'll go and how much a detour has to save before it's worth it.
- The price you actually pay. Enter your fuel discounts once. Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's and cardlock stations only show up if you have a membership.
### Motorhomes and big fifth wheels
With FuelPilot Big Rig, set your vehicle type to RV / motorhome and enter its height, weight and length. Routes then clear your rig's size, avoiding low bridges, weight limits and restricted roads, and every fuel station still shows so you can pick the one that suits you. Truck routes depend on map data and the sizes you enter, so always follow posted signs and use your own judgment. Big Rig is on iPhone now and comes to Android in the next update.
### What it costs
Navigation and the cheapest gas near you are free. Towing mode and Autopilot come with FuelPilot Pro, $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year. RV routing for your rig's size comes with Big Rig, $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year, which includes everything in Pro. Both start with a 7-day free trial. FuelPilot works in the United States and Canada.
### Free tools
Work out how far you can go between stops with the towing range calculator, or read how to plan fuel stops when towing.
### Questions
#### How far can I tow on a tank of fuel?
Multiply your usable tank size by your towing MPG, then keep a reserve. A 36-gallon tank at 9 MPG towing is 324 miles, and keeping a quarter tank in reserve leaves about 243 miles between stops. Towing MPG varies with weight, wind, hills and speed, which is why FuelPilot learns your real MPG from your fill-ups instead of using the window sticker.
#### What's the best app for planning fuel stops while towing a travel trailer?
Look for an app that plans stops from your towing range, not just one that lists prices nearby. FuelPilot does that: it adjusts your range for the trailer, picks the cheapest stations you can reach along the route and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions.
#### Will FuelPilot route my motorhome around low bridges?
Yes, with FuelPilot Big Rig and your RV's height, weight and length entered. Without Big Rig, routes are planned for a passenger vehicle and don't account for bridge heights or weight limits, and the app tells you the route hasn't been checked for your vehicle's size.
#### Does FuelPilot show diesel prices?
Yes. FuelPilot shows prices for the fuel your vehicle uses, including diesel, from HERE Technologies. Prices can lag behind the pump, so the price on the pump is the one you pay.
#### Can I plan a trip with FuelPilot before I leave?
Yes. Pick a destination and choose between routes. With Pro, Autopilot shows every planned fuel stop in the route preview, and you tap Add stops to add them.
#### Does it work for a diesel pickup that isn't towing?
Yes. Each vehicle keeps its own settings, so you can plan with your normal range when the trailer's off and switch towing mode on when you hitch up.

## Big Rig, for truckers (https://fuelpilotapp.com/big-rig/)

### Truck GPS that plans your fuel stops
FuelPilot Big Rig plans truck-legal routes for your rig's height, weight and length, sends you only to truck stops and truck lanes at the truck-lane diesel price, and picks the cheapest stop you can reach. Every trip is logged with miles by state for IFTA. For semis, hot shots and RVs.
### What Big Rig does
- Truck-legal routes. Enter your rig's height, weight and length, plus axles, trailers and hazmat. Routes avoid low bridges, weight limits, restricted roads and hazmat restrictions. Any box you leave blank uses a typical semi: 13'6", 80,000 lb and 72 ft.
- Truck stops and truck lanes only. For a semi or hot shot, fuel stops are truck stops and truck lanes, priced at the truck-lane diesel price.
- Fuel Autopilot. Every fuel stop for the run, picked before you leave from prices along the whole route and the range you really have. After each fill-up it checks the next stop still makes sense.
- The road ahead. A list of what's coming up on your route: your fuel stops, truck stops, weigh stations, rest areas, restrictions, and weather and road alerts. Weigh stations on your route also show on the map.
- IFTA summary. Export a quarterly summary with miles and gallons by state, worked out from the GPS path of the trips you navigated and the receipts you scanned.
- Receipts read for you. Photograph a receipt and the station, gallons, price and total fill themselves in.
- One app for the truck and the car. Switch Big Rig mode off on the map to get car routes and every gas station, and back on for the truck.
Truck routes depend on map data and the sizes you enter, so always follow posted signs and use your own judgment. If truck routing can't be reached, FuelPilot shows the car route and warns you before you start and while you drive. If no legal truck route exists for a trip, it tells you instead of routing.
### What it costs
Big Rig is $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year in the US and includes everything in FuelPilot Pro. It starts with a 7-day free trial. Big Rig is on iPhone now and comes to Android in the next update. FuelPilot works in the United States and Canada.
### Free tools
See what every mile costs you with the hot shot cost per mile calculator, compare Trucker Path alternatives, or read about IFTA mileage log apps.
### Questions
#### Is there a truck GPS app that also plans fuel stops?
Yes. FuelPilot Big Rig combines truck-legal routing with fuel planning: it picks the cheapest truck stops and truck lanes you can reach along a truck-legal route, adds them to your directions and logs the miles for IFTA.
#### Does FuelPilot work for hot shot trucks?
Yes. Set your vehicle type to Hot shot / HD pickup and enter its height, weight and length. Routes follow truck-legal roads and fuel stops are truck stops and truck lanes at the truck-lane diesel price.
#### Can FuelPilot do my IFTA miles by state?
It works them out for you. Miles by state come from the GPS path of the trips you navigated with FuelPilot, checked against official state boundaries, and fuel by state comes from where your receipts were scanned. Export the quarterly summary as a spreadsheet. Drives you didn't navigate with FuelPilot aren't included, so check the totals before you file.
#### Does it avoid hazmat-restricted roads?
Yes. Mark your load as hazmat in your vehicle settings and Big Rig routes avoid hazmat restrictions.
#### Does FuelPilot show weigh stations?
Yes, with Big Rig. Weigh stations on your route show on the map and in the road-ahead list, along with your fuel stops, truck stops, rest areas, and weather and road alerts. It doesn't show whether a scale is open right now.
#### Can I use it in my own car on the weekend?
Yes. Turn off the Big Rig switch on the map or in Settings and you get car routes and every gas station again.

## Mileage log (https://fuelpilotapp.com/mileage-log/)

### A mileage log that fills itself in
Every drive you navigate with FuelPilot is saved to your logbook with its route, miles, time and fuel. Tag it business or personal, add a note, and export a mileage log or fuel expense report when tax time comes. FuelPilot also plans your fuel stops at the cheapest station you can reach, so the trip costs less in the first place.
### What gets logged
- Every navigated drive. The route map, miles, time, MPG, stops and what you saved on fuel, saved automatically when you drive with FuelPilot's directions.
- Business or personal. Tag each trip and add notes, such as the client or job it was for.
- Fuel receipts. Photograph a receipt and, with Pro, the station, gallons, price and total are read for you. You can always type them in yourself.
- More than one vehicle. With Pro, add every vehicle you drive, each with its own tank size and MPG.
### Exports
With FuelPilot Pro, open the Trips tab, tap Export and choose a mileage log, a fuel expense report or a quarterly IFTA summary for the period you need. You get a spreadsheet (CSV) file and a private download link that works for 24 hours, so you can email it to your accountant or open it on a computer.
### What it costs
The logbook is free for your last 7 days. Older trips are kept, and they all come back if you upgrade. Pro is $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year in the US, starts with a 7-day free trial, and adds the full logbook, exports, receipt reading and Fuel Autopilot. FuelPilot works in the United States and Canada.
### Compare
See how FuelPilot stacks up as a mileage log in FuelPilot vs MileIQ vs Everlance, and how to track miles by state in IFTA mileage log apps.
### Questions
#### Does FuelPilot track my mileage automatically?
It logs every drive you navigate with FuelPilot, with no extra taps. It doesn't record drives you make without starting directions in the app, so start a route for each work trip you want in the log.
#### Can I export a mileage log for my taxes?
Yes, with FuelPilot Pro. Export a mileage log or a fuel expense report as a spreadsheet for any period and send it to your accountant. Ask your tax preparer what your records need to show for your situation.
#### What's a good mileage tracker app that also saves money on gas?
FuelPilot does both: it logs the drives you navigate for your records, and its Autopilot plans each fuel stop at the cheapest station you can reach on your route.
#### Does it work for gig and delivery drivers?
Yes, for the drives you navigate with FuelPilot. Tag each one business or personal and export the log when you need it.
#### Can it do IFTA for a hot shot or semi?
Yes. The quarterly IFTA summary has miles and gallons by state, worked out from the GPS path of the trips you navigated and the receipts you scanned. See FuelPilot for truckers.

## Support and FAQ (https://fuelpilotapp.com/support/)

### Support
Answers to common questions. If yours isn't here, email support@fuelpilotapp.com and we'll get back to you, usually within a day or two.
### Getting started
#### What do I need to set up first?
Allow location when FuelPilot asks, then add your vehicle in the Vehicle tab with its tank size and MPG. Range and fuel stop picks depend on those two numbers, and FuelPilot learns your real MPG as you log fill-ups. Set the fuel gauge in the app to match your tank before a trip.
#### Do I need an account?
No. Tap Continue without an account on the sign-in screen to use the app right away. Signing out as a guest deletes your vehicles, trips and receipts, so create an account in Settings first if you want to keep them. Fuel prices along your route, FuelPilot Pro and Big Rig need an account.
#### Do I need an OBD-II adapter?
No. There's nothing to plug in. FuelPilot plans from your tank size, the fuel level you set and the MPG it learns from your fill-ups.
#### Is FuelPilot on Android?
Yes. FuelPilot is on Google Play. A few newer features, including Big Rig, come to Android in the next update.
### Fuel prices and Autopilot
#### Where do the fuel prices come from?
From HERE Technologies, a fuel price provider, and they're refreshed regularly. Prices can still lag behind the pump, so the price on the pump is the one you pay.
#### Why didn't Autopilot pick the cheapest station I can see?
Autopilot picks the cheapest station you can reach with your reserve left, on or close to your route. A cheaper station might be out of range, too far off the route, or not save enough to be worth the detour. You can change your reserve and the minimum savings for a detour in Settings › Autopilot.
#### How does Autopilot plan a long trip?
It plans every fuel stop for the whole trip before you leave and shows them in the route preview. Tap Add stops to add them. After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense, and changes it if prices or your range have moved. You can turn partial fills on or off and set the smallest fill in Settings.
#### I get a discount at some stations.
Enter it once in Settings › My discounts. FuelPilot then compares stations using the price you actually pay.
#### A station is closed, or the price is wrong.
Open the station and report it. Your own map changes right away. Other drivers see the change once reports from the station itself confirm it.
#### Why doesn't it send me to Costco or a cardlock?
Stations that need a membership are left out until you tell FuelPilot you have one. Turn on Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's or fleet cardlock in Settings › Fuel memberships.
### Navigation
#### Does FuelPilot avoid low bridges and truck restrictions?
With FuelPilot Big Rig, yes. Set your vehicle's type and its height, weight and length, and Big Rig plans truck-legal routes around low bridges, weight limits and restricted roads, and only sends you to truck stops and truck lanes. Truck routes depend on map data and the sizes you enter, so always follow posted signs and use your own judgment. Without Big Rig, routes are planned for passenger vehicles and don't account for bridge heights, weight limits or truck restrictions.
#### How do I set up my truck or RV?
In the Vehicle tab, edit the vehicle and set its type to RV / motorhome, Hot shot / HD pickup or Semi, then enter its height, weight and length. For a truck you can also enter axles, trailers and hazmat. Any box you leave blank uses a typical size: a semi is 13'6", 80,000 lb and 72 ft. Truck and RV routes need FuelPilot Big Rig. If Big Rig mode is on and your vehicle is still set to Car / pickup, routes are planned for a typical semi.
#### What changes when Big Rig mode is on?
For a semi or hot shot, routes follow truck-legal roads and avoid low bridges, weight limits and hazmat restrictions, fuel stops are truck stops and truck lanes only at the truck-lane diesel price, and Food is left out of the quick stops. For an RV, routes clear its height, weight and length, and every station still shows. The top of the map says Truck routes with your rig's size, and the route preview says Truck route.
#### How do I go back to car routes?
Turn off the Big Rig switch on the bar at the top of the map, or in Settings › Big Rig. You get car routes and every gas station again. Turn it back on any time. If a route is on screen, it's planned again for the new mode.
#### What does "Not a truck route" mean?
Truck routing couldn't be reached, so FuelPilot is showing the normal car route and warning you before you start and while you drive. That route hasn't been checked for your rig's size, so check it yourself, or plan the route again in a moment. If no legal truck route exists for a trip, FuelPilot tells you instead of routing.
#### What does "Car route — not checked" mean?
Your vehicle is set up as an RV or truck, but you don't have FuelPilot Big Rig, so the route is planned for a car and isn't checked against your vehicle's size.
#### Can I avoid tolls or highways?
Yes. Turn on Avoid tolls or Avoid highways in Settings. When there's more than one way to go, the route preview lets you choose between routes.
#### Does FuelPilot work with CarPlay?
Not yet. CarPlay is built and will be turned on in a later update.
#### Directions stop when my screen locks.
On your iPhone, open Settings › FuelPilot › Location, choose Always and turn on Precise Location. FuelPilot only uses your location in the background while you're navigating.
#### The spoken directions sound robotic.
FuelPilot uses the best voice installed on your iPhone. To download a better one, open Settings › Accessibility › Spoken Content › Voices, pick English and download an Enhanced or Premium voice. Then choose it in FuelPilot's Settings.
### Trips and exports
#### How are trips recorded?
Every drive you navigate with FuelPilot is saved to your logbook automatically. The free plan shows the last 7 days. Older trips are kept, and they all come back if you upgrade to Pro.
#### How do I export a mileage log or IFTA report?
In the Trips tab, tap Export, choose a mileage log, fuel expense report or IFTA summary, and pick the period. You get a spreadsheet (CSV) file and a private download link that works for 24 hours, so you can email it or open it on a computer. Exports are part of FuelPilot Pro.
#### How does the IFTA summary work out miles by state?
From the GPS path of the trips you navigated with FuelPilot, checked against official state boundaries, and fuel by state from where your receipts were scanned. Drives you didn't navigate with FuelPilot aren't included, so check the totals before you file.
### Receipts
#### How do I log a fuel-up?
Tap Add receipt and take a photo of the receipt. With FuelPilot Pro, the station, gallons, price and total are read from the photo for you to check and confirm. You can always type the details in yourself.
#### Can I stop receipt photos being read by AI?
Yes. Turn off Read receipts with AI in Settings › Receipts. Photos are then only stored with your receipt, and you enter the numbers yourself.
### FuelPilot Pro and Big Rig
#### What does Pro include, and how much is it?
Fuel Autopilot, which picks and adds every fuel stop for your trip, plus receipt reading, your full logbook with exports, and more than one vehicle with towing mode. A free account still shows fuel prices along your route. It's $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year in the US, and starts with a 7-day free trial.
#### What is Big Rig, and how much is it?
Big Rig is the plan for semis, hot shots and RVs. It plans truck-legal routes for your rig's height, weight and length, and only sends you to truck stops and truck lanes, at the truck-lane diesel price. Everything in Pro is included. It's $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year in the US, and starts with a 7-day free trial. Switch Big Rig mode off on the map or in Settings any time to drive a car.
#### How do I switch between Pro and Big Rig?
Open Settings › Subscription and use the Pro / Big Rig switch at the top. They're in the same subscription group, so moving from Pro to Big Rig is an upgrade through Apple, not a second subscription. To go from Big Rig back to Pro, change the plan in your iPhone's subscription settings.
#### How do I cancel?
On your iPhone, open Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions, tap FuelPilot and then Cancel Subscription. Cancel at least 24 hours before your trial or billing period ends to avoid the next charge. Deleting the app or your account doesn't cancel the subscription.
On Android, open the Play Store, tap your profile picture, then Payments & subscriptions › Subscriptions, pick FuelPilot and tap Cancel subscription.
#### I got a new phone and my plan is gone.
Sign in to FuelPilot, open Settings › Subscription and tap Restore Purchases. Make sure your phone is signed in to the same Apple Account you used to subscribe.
#### How do I get a refund?
Apple handles payments and refunds for the App Store. Request one at reportaproblem.apple.com.
### Your account
#### I forgot my password.
On the sign-in screen, tap Forgot password? and enter your email. We'll send you a 6-digit code to type into the app, then you choose a new password. Check your spam folder if it doesn't arrive.
#### How do I delete my account?
In the app, open Settings › Profile › Delete account. This permanently deletes your account and all its data. If you can't sign in, see Delete your account.
### Still need help?
Email us and include your phone model and iOS version.
support@fuelpilotapp.com

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/best-gas-apps-for-road-trips/)

### The best gas apps for road trips, and what each one is for
November 25, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
No single app does everything on a road trip. Use GasBuddy or iExit to see prices, Upside to get cash back at the pump, Kibi to pick exits with food and clean bathrooms, Roadtrippers to plan the sights, and FuelPilot to plan every fuel stop from your tank and drive you there. Here's what each is best at, so you can pick two or three that cover you.
I make FuelPilot, so weigh that. Prices and features are as listed on each app's store page or website in November 2026.
### At a glance
- App | Best for | Cost
- FuelPilot | Planning every fuel stop from your tank and real MPG, with turn-by-turn directions | Free; Pro $7.99/mo or $49.99/yr
- GasBuddy | Crowd-reported gas prices and a discount card | Free; paid plans from $7.99/mo
- iExit | What's at the exits ahead, and the cheapest gas at each one | Free
- Upside | Cash back at participating stations | Free
- Kibi | Exits with gas, food and a clean bathroom in one stop | Free with in-app purchases; iPhone only
- Roadtrippers | Planning the route and the places to see | Free tier and paid plans
- Google Maps, Waze | Directions, traffic, and finding a station on the fly | Free
### FuelPilot: plans the fuel stops for you
Most gas apps show you prices and leave the math to you: how far you can get on this tank, which cheap station you can actually reach, and whether a detour is worth it. FuelPilot does that part. It knows your tank size, learns your real MPG from your fill-ups and checks prices along the whole route. With Pro, Autopilot picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the trip, keeping the reserve you choose, and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions. Towing mode adjusts your range when you hitch up a trailer.
Good to know: prices come from HERE Technologies, not users. There's no CarPlay yet and no discount card. Navigation and the cheapest gas near you are free; Autopilot needs Pro.
### GasBuddy: the biggest price map
GasBuddy's users report prices as they fill up, so it covers most towns well. Pay with GasBuddy is a payment card that takes money off each gallon, and its Plus and Premium plans save 20¢ a gallon on your first 50 gallons each month. If you want to know what every station in town charges, start here. FuelPilot vs GasBuddy goes into more detail.
### iExit: what's at the next exit
iExit follows you down the interstate and shows what's at each exit ahead: gas, food, hotels, rest areas, EV chargers and RV or truck parking. It shows the cheapest gas at each exit, so you can compare the exits coming up. It works with CarPlay.
### Upside: cash back on the fill-up
Upside is a free app that gives cash back at participating gas stations, grocery stores and restaurants. Claim an offer in the app before you pay, then pay as usual with your card. Gas offers can reach 25¢ a gallon, but they vary by station and day. It works only in the US.
### Kibi: exits with everything you need
Kibi plans stops where you can get gas, food and a clean bathroom at one exit, timed to your car's fuel range with a safety buffer. It scores more than 79,000 US highway exits, then hands your stops to Google Maps, Apple Maps or Waze. It's iPhone only, and it describes itself as not a turn-by-turn app and not a gas price tracker. If a good bathroom matters more than saving 20¢ a gallon, Kibi is a strong pick.
### Roadtrippers: plan the trip, not just the fuel
Roadtrippers is a route planner for finding attractions, campgrounds and places to stay along the way. It has a free tier and paid plans with extras like offline maps and RV tools. Use it to decide where you're going and what you'll see. It doesn't plan fuel stops around your tank.
### Google Maps and Waze
Free, familiar and good at traffic. Both let you search for gas stations along your route and show prices for many of them. Neither knows how far your tank will go, so picking the stop is still up to you.
### A good road trip setup
- Long trip, want it cheap and planned: FuelPilot, plus Upside for cash back where there's an offer.
- Family trip with kids: Kibi for food and bathroom stops, and GasBuddy or iExit for prices.
- Towing a camper: FuelPilot with towing mode, and Roadtrippers for campgrounds. See how to plan fuel stops when towing.
- Short trip, free only: Google Maps or Waze, and GasBuddy.
Want a number before you leave? The trip fuel cost calculator works out the fuel cost of any trip.
### Questions
#### What is the best gas app for a road trip?
It depends on the job. GasBuddy has the widest price coverage, Upside gives cash back at participating stations, iExit shows the cheapest gas at each exit ahead, and FuelPilot plans every fuel stop for the trip from your tank and real MPG and gives you directions there.
#### Is there an app that plans gas stops for a road trip?
Yes. FuelPilot plans fuel stops at the cheapest stations you can reach with your range and reserve, and adds them to its turn-by-turn directions. Kibi plans exits with gas, food and a clean bathroom around your fuel range and hands them to your maps app.
#### Can I use GasBuddy and Upside together?
They're separate apps, so you can have both. Use GasBuddy to compare prices and Upside to see which nearby stations have a cash back offer. Whether a GasBuddy card discount and an Upside offer both apply to the same fill-up depends on each app's terms, so check before you count on it.
#### Do Google Maps and Waze show gas prices?
Both show prices for many stations when you search for gas along your route. Neither plans stops around how far your tank will go.
David Kulagin is a diesel mechanic who hauls for work. He founded Ghost Systems LLC, which makes FuelPilot.

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/fuelpilot-vs-mileiq-vs-everlance/)

### Mileage tracker apps for work: FuelPilot vs MileIQ vs Everlance
November 25, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
MileIQ and Everlance log your drives automatically in the background, whether or not you open them. FuelPilot logs the drives you navigate with it, and also plans your fuel stops and tracks fuel expenses. If you want every drive caught without thinking about it, pick MileIQ or Everlance. If most of your work driving is trips you'd use directions for anyway, and fuel is a big cost, FuelPilot does both jobs.
I make FuelPilot, so weigh that. Prices are US prices from each company's site in November 2026.
### Why it matters
For 2026, the IRS standard mileage rate for business use is 72.5 cents a mile. At that rate, 10,000 business miles is a $7,250 deduction, so missed trips cost real money. Whatever app you use, the log has to be one you'll actually keep up. Ask your tax preparer what your records need to show.
### At a glance
- MileIQ | Everlance | FuelPilot
- How drives are logged | Detected automatically | Detected automatically | Every drive you navigate in the app
- Free plan | 40 drives a month | 30 automatic trips a month, plus unlimited manual trips | Last 7 days of trips
- Paid plan | Unlimited: $7.50/mo billed yearly, or $8.99 monthly | Starter: $8.99/mo or $69.99/yr | Pro: $7.99/mo or $49.99/yr
- Navigation | No | No | Turn-by-turn, with fuel stops planned
- Fuel expenses | Not its focus | Expense tracking with receipts | Receipt photos read for you; fuel expense report
- IFTA miles by state | No | No | Quarterly IFTA summary (Pro)
### MileIQ
Best for: anyone who wants every drive logged without touching the app.
MileIQ runs in the background and detects drives on its own. You swipe each one business or personal and it builds the reports. The free plan covers 40 drives a month; Unlimited is $7.50 a month billed yearly or $8.99 month to month.
### Everlance
Best for: self-employed drivers who want mileage and other business expenses in one place.
Everlance also detects trips automatically. The free Basic plan includes 30 automatic trips a month and unlimited manual trips. Starter, with unlimited automatic tracking, is $8.99 a month or $69.99 a year, and a Professional plan is $99.99 a year.
### FuelPilot
Best for: drivers who navigate to their jobs and spend a lot on fuel.
- Every drive you navigate with FuelPilot is saved with its route, miles, time and fuel. Tag it business or personal and add a note, like the client or job.
- Photograph a fuel receipt and, with Pro, the station, gallons, price and total are read for you.
- Export a mileage log, a fuel expense report or a quarterly IFTA summary as a spreadsheet.
- Autopilot plans each fuel stop at the cheapest station you can reach, so the drive costs less in the first place.
The catch: FuelPilot doesn't detect drives on its own. A drive you make without starting directions in the app isn't logged. If you often hop in the truck without navigating, you'll miss trips.
### Which one to pick
- Lots of short local drives, no navigation: MileIQ or Everlance.
- You want receipts and other expenses too: Everlance.
- Long work drives you navigate anyway, a diesel truck, or IFTA: FuelPilot. One yearly Pro plan covers the log, the fuel stops and the exports.
- Both: some drivers use a background tracker for the log and FuelPilot for the fuel planning.
### Questions
#### What is the IRS mileage rate for 2026?
The IRS standard mileage rate for business use of a car, van, pickup or panel truck is 72.5 cents a mile for 2026, up 2.5 cents from 2025.
#### Does FuelPilot track mileage automatically like MileIQ?
Not in the same way. MileIQ detects drives in the background. FuelPilot logs every drive you navigate with it, with no extra taps, but doesn't record drives where you didn't start directions in the app.
#### Which mileage app is cheapest?
Each has a free plan: MileIQ covers 40 drives a month, Everlance 30 automatic trips a month plus manual trips, and FuelPilot your last 7 days of trips. On paid plans, FuelPilot Pro is $49.99 a year, Everlance Starter $69.99 a year and MileIQ Unlimited $7.50 a month billed yearly.
#### Is there a mileage tracker that also saves money on gas?
FuelPilot logs the drives you navigate and plans each fuel stop at the cheapest station you can reach on your route.
#### Which app works for IFTA?
Of these three, only FuelPilot exports a quarterly IFTA summary with miles and gallons by state. See IFTA mileage tracking apps for owner-operators.

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/ifta-mileage-tracking-app/)

### IFTA mileage log apps for owner-operators and hot shots
November 25, 2026 · Updated November 27, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
Your IFTA return needs your miles in every state and the fuel you bought in each. If you run an ELD, check whether it already reports miles by state. If you don't, a phone app can do it: GPS apps like IFTA Track log state miles as you drive, manual apps like IFTA Ledger do the quarterly math from what you enter, and FuelPilot works out state miles from the trips you navigate and the receipts you scan, and also plans your fuel stops.
I make FuelPilot, so weigh that. This isn't tax advice. Your base state's IFTA office has the final word on what your records need to show.
### Do you need IFTA?
You need an IFTA license if you run a qualified motor vehicle in more than one IFTA state or province. Under the agreement, a qualified motor vehicle carries people or property and:
- has two axles and a gross or registered gross weight over 26,000 lb, or
- has three or more axles, regardless of weight, or
- is used in combination with a total weight over 26,000 lb.
That last line is the one that catches hot shots. A one-ton pickup and gooseneck rated over 26,000 lb together qualify, even though the pickup alone doesn't. Recreational vehicles are not qualified motor vehicles.
### When returns are due
Returns are filed quarterly with your base state, by the last day of the month after each quarter:
- January to March: April 30
- April to June: July 31
- July to September: October 31
- October to December: January 31
### What your records need
For each quarter you report total miles and the miles in each state, and the fuel you bought in each state. IFTA licensees have to keep records that back up every return, and you can be audited. In practice that means trip records showing where you drove and your fuel receipts. Ask your base state what it accepts as the source of your miles before you rely on an app alone.
### Your options
- Option | How miles get logged | Cost (Nov 2026)
- Your ELD | From the truck, if your ELD offers IFTA reports | Part of your ELD plan, if included
- FuelPilot | GPS path of trips you navigate; fuel from scanned receipts | Pro $49.99/yr (Big Rig $199.99/yr adds truck routing)
- IFTA Track | Phone GPS in the background | Free with in-app purchases
- IFTA Ledger | You enter miles and fuel by state | $14.99 once
- Paper or spreadsheet | Odometer at each state line | Free, but slow
### Your ELD
If you already run an ELD, look for an IFTA or state mileage report in it first. It's the least extra work. If you're exempt from the ELD rule, as some short-haul operations are, you'll need another way.
### FuelPilot
Every trip you navigate with FuelPilot is logged, and miles by state are worked out from the GPS path, checked against official state boundaries. Photograph a fuel receipt and the station, gallons and price are read for you, and the state comes from where it was scanned. With Pro, export a quarterly IFTA summary with miles and gallons by state as a spreadsheet.
It also does the thing the IFTA apps don't: Autopilot picks the cheapest fuel stop you can reach for every stop on the run. With Big Rig, routes are truck-legal for your rig's height, weight and length, and fuel stops are truck stops and truck lanes. There's a Hot shot / HD pickup vehicle type.
The catch: drives you don't navigate with FuelPilot aren't included. Navigate every loaded and empty leg, and check the totals before you file.
### IFTA Track
IFTA Track uses your phone's GPS to log miles by state or province automatically, and builds summary reports with miles and taxable gallons by jurisdiction. It's free to download with in-app purchases. It needs an internet connection and runs location in the background, which uses battery.
### IFTA Ledger
If you'd rather enter numbers yourself, IFTA Ledger is a trip log and IFTA calculator that works offline. You log miles and fuel by state and it builds the quarterly summary. Everything unlocks for a one-time $14.99.
### Paper and odometer
Write down the odometer at every state line, plus each fuel purchase. It's free and auditors know it, but it's easy to miss a line and slow to total up every quarter.
### Our take
- You have an ELD with IFTA reports: use it, and keep your fuel receipts.
- You want to set it and forget it: a background GPS app.
- You want state miles and cheaper fuel from one app: FuelPilot, as long as you navigate every leg with it.
See what your miles really cost with the hot shot cost per mile calculator.
### Questions
#### Does a hot shot truck need IFTA?
If the truck and trailer together weigh or are registered over 26,000 lb and you run in more than one IFTA state or province, yes. The combination rule counts the trailer, so a pickup that doesn't qualify alone can qualify with a gooseneck behind it.
#### When are IFTA returns due?
Quarterly, by the last day of the month after the quarter ends: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31.
#### Can I use a phone app to track IFTA miles?
Yes. Apps can log miles by state from your phone's GPS or work them out from your routes. Keep your fuel receipts and the trip records behind the totals, and check with your base state what records it expects in an audit.
#### Does FuelPilot do IFTA?
Yes, with FuelPilot Pro or Big Rig. It works out miles by state from the GPS path of the trips you navigate and gallons by state from your scanned receipts, and exports a quarterly summary as a spreadsheet. Drives you don't navigate with FuelPilot aren't included.
#### Do RVs need IFTA?
No. Recreational vehicles are not qualified motor vehicles under IFTA.
David Kulagin is a diesel mechanic who hauls for work. He founded Ghost Systems LLC, which makes FuelPilot.

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/how-to-plan-fuel-stops-when-towing/)

### How to plan fuel stops when towing a travel trailer or fifth wheel, and the best apps for it
November 25, 2026 · Updated November 27, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
Work out your real towing MPG, multiply it by your usable tank, keep a quarter tank in reserve, and plan a stop before every stretch where stations are far apart. Then pick stations you can get a trailer in and out of, and check the plan again after every fill-up. The best app for it is one that plans from your towing range, not just one that lists prices: compare the apps.
### 1. Find your real towing MPG
The number on your dash when you're not towing is no use here. A trailer is heavy and it's a wall of air behind your truck. When the Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory tested an SUV pulling a 3,500 lb enclosed cargo trailer, fuel economy dropped by about 30% in city driving and by about 50% at 80 mph. A big travel trailer or fifth wheel can do the same or worse.
The way to know your number is the fill-up method:
- Fill the tank and reset your trip meter.
- Tow as you normally would.
- At the next fill-up, divide the miles driven by the gallons it took to fill back up.
Do it over two or three tanks and take the average. Your truck's MPG readout can be off, and one tank into a headwind will make you think it's worse than it is.
### 2. Work out your range, and keep a reserve
Range is usable tank size times towing MPG. A 36-gallon tank at 9 MPG towing is 324 miles. Don't plan to use all of it. Keep a quarter tank in reserve and you've got about 243 miles between stops.
The reserve is for the things you can't plan: a closed station, a pump that won't take your card, a detour, a long climb, a headwind. The towing range calculator does this math for your rig.
### 3. Plan around the long empty stretches
In most of the East you'll pass a station every few miles. In parts of the West and in rural Canada you can go well over 100 miles without one. Look at the whole route before you leave and mark the gaps. Fill up before every gap that's longer than your range after reserve, even if the tank isn't low yet. Fuel there may cost more. Running out costs more.
### 4. Slow down
Air drag climbs fast with speed, and a trailer adds a lot of it. That's why the Oak Ridge test lost so much more at 80 mph than around town. Dropping your cruising speed is the easiest way to stretch your range while towing. Many trailer tires are also rated for lower speeds than car tires, so check the sidewall.
### 5. Pick stations you can get out of
The cheapest station on the map is no good if you can't swing a 35-foot trailer through it. Before you commit to a stop:
- Check it on satellite view. Look for pumps you can pull straight through and an exit that doesn't need a tight turn.
- Prefer the outside pumps, with room to pull forward when you're done.
- For diesel, many larger stations and travel centers have diesel at the car pumps or separate lanes that fit an RV. Truck lanes are built for semis, so check the station's rules before you pull in.
- Plan your stops when you'd want a break anyway. A fuel stop is a good time for a walk-around: hitch, safety chains, lights and tire pressures.
### 6. Check the plan after every fill-up
Things change once you're moving. Wind, hills and traffic change your real MPG, and prices change through the day. Every time you fill up, look at the next stretch again and decide where the next stop is.
### The best apps to plan fuel stops when towing
I make FuelPilot, so weigh that. Most towing setups use two or three of these together. Prices are US prices as listed by each company in November 2026.
- App | Best for when towing | Cost
- FuelPilot | Plans every fuel stop from your towing range, picks the cheapest stations you can reach and drives you there | Free; towing mode and Autopilot with Pro, $7.99/mo or $49.99/yr
- RV LIFE Trip Wizard | Planning an RV trip: RV-safe routes and campgrounds | Part of RV LIFE Pro, $65/yr or $19.99/mo
- Trucker Path | Truck stops, diesel prices and parking for big rigs | Free; fuel plans with Diamond, $29.99/mo
- iExit | What's at each exit ahead, including the cheapest gas and RV parking | Free
- GasBuddy | Comparing prices in a town | Free; paid plans from $7.99/mo
- Pilot Flying J, Love's, TA apps | Locations and loyalty discounts at those chains | Free
- FuelPilot is the one built around the math in this guide. Towing mode cuts your range for the trailer, it learns your real towing MPG from your fill-ups, and Autopilot puts the stops into your turn-by-turn directions with the reserve you choose.
- RV LIFE Trip Wizard comes with an RV LIFE Pro membership, along with RV-safe navigation in the RV LIFE app and campground reviews. Use it to decide where you're camping each night.
- Trucker Path is made for semi drivers. It's handy if you pull a big fifth wheel and want truck stops with diesel prices, but its fuel plans need the Diamond plan, and truck lanes aren't always open to RVs.
- iExit follows you down the interstate and shows what's at each exit coming up. It's a good way to check the stops ahead while you drive.
- GasBuddy has the biggest crowd-reported price map. It doesn't know your range or whether a station fits a trailer, so check before you pull in. See FuelPilot vs GasBuddy.
- Chain apps from Pilot Flying J, Love's and TA show their own stations and give loyalty discounts. They're worth having once you know roughly where you'll stop.
### Let an app do the planning
Doing all of this by hand works. It also means stopping to do math while you're towing. FuelPilot does it for you:
- Towing mode adjusts your range for the trailer, and FuelPilot learns your real MPG from your fill-ups.
- Autopilot picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the whole trip, keeping the reserve you choose, and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions.
- After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense.
- With Big Rig, routes clear your motorhome's height, weight and length.
Towing mode and Autopilot come with FuelPilot Pro, $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year with a 7-day free trial. More about towing with FuelPilot.
### Questions
#### How much does towing a travel trailer reduce gas mileage?
It depends on the trailer's weight and shape and how fast you drive. In a Department of Energy test at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, an SUV towing a 3,500 lb enclosed trailer lost about 30% of its fuel economy in city driving and about 50% at 80 mph. Measure your own with the fill-up method over two or three tanks.
#### How often should I stop for fuel when towing?
Plan stops from your range after reserve. Multiply your usable tank by your towing MPG, then take off a quarter tank. A 36-gallon tank at 9 MPG gives about 243 miles between stops. Stop earlier before any stretch with no stations.
#### How much fuel should I keep in reserve when towing?
A quarter tank is a common rule. It covers a closed station, a detour or a headwind. Keep more in remote areas or in winter.
#### Can I use truck stop diesel lanes with a fifth wheel?
Some stations allow it and some don't. Truck lanes are built for semis, so check the station's rules first. Many larger stations and travel centers have diesel at car pumps or lanes that fit an RV.
#### What's the best app for planning fuel stops while towing?
Look for one that plans from your towing range, not just one that lists prices. FuelPilot adjusts your range for the trailer, learns your real towing MPG, picks the cheapest stations you can reach along the route and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions. Many RVers pair it with RV LIFE Trip Wizard for campgrounds, and with iExit, GasBuddy or a chain app like Love's or Pilot Flying J for prices and discounts.
#### Is there an app that plans fuel stops for towing a camper?
Yes. FuelPilot has a towing mode: it plans every fuel stop for the trip from your range with the trailer on, keeps the reserve you choose and navigates you to each stop. Towing mode comes with FuelPilot Pro, $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year with a 7-day free trial. You can work out your range by hand with the free towing range calculator.

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/trucker-path-alternatives/)

### Trucker Path alternatives: free and paid truck GPS and fuel apps compared
November 25, 2026 · Updated November 27, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
Trucker Path is the app most drivers already have, and its Diamond plan plans fuel stops too. If you're an owner-operator paying for your own fuel, the questions are what that costs, what else you need, and whether another app does the job for less. Here are the main alternatives, what each is best at, and where Trucker Path is still the better pick.
I make FuelPilot, one of the apps on this list, so weigh that. Prices are US prices as listed on each company's site or the App Store in November 2026. They change, so check before you buy.
### First: what Trucker Path already does
The free app covers truck stops, fuel prices, parking, weigh station status history, a load board and a big driver community. The Diamond plan, $29.99 a month, $149.99 for six months or $249.99 a year with a 7-day trial, adds CarPlay, trips with more than three stops, HOS rest reminders and Smart Fuel Plans, which work out where to stop and how much to put in. Any user can also buy discounted fuel through the app.
So if you need parking and a fuel plan in one app and the price is fine with you, Trucker Path Diamond may be all you need. The alternatives below make sense when you want something cheaper, something free, or something that also covers your pickup, your RV or your IFTA miles.
### The alternatives at a glance
- App | Price (Nov 2026) | Best for
- FuelPilot Big Rig | $19.99/mo or $199.99/yr | Fuel stops planned for you, IFTA miles, one app for the truck and the car
- Hammer | Free | Free truck GPS with offline maps
- CoPilot Truck | $9.99/mo or $119.99/yr | Offline truck navigation
- Mudflap | Free | Diesel discounts at independent truck stops
- TruckMap | Free | A free map of truck stops, weigh stations and parking
- Sygic Truck & RV | Paid subscription | Offline truck and RV navigation in North America and Europe
### FuelPilot Big Rig
Best for: owner-operators and hot shot drivers who want every fuel stop planned from their real range, and their IFTA miles worked out from the trips they drive.
- Truck-legal routes for your rig's height, weight and length, plus axles, trailers and hazmat.
- Fuel Autopilot picks the cheapest truck stop or truck lane you can reach for every stop on the run, before you leave, and re-checks after each fill-up. It plans at the truck-lane diesel price.
- It learns your real MPG from your fill-ups. No OBD-II adapter or ELD connection needed.
- A quarterly IFTA summary with miles and gallons by state, from the GPS path of the trips you navigated and the receipts you scanned. Drives you don't navigate with FuelPilot aren't included.
- A road-ahead list of your fuel stops, truck stops, weigh stations, rest areas, and weather and road alerts.
- Switch Big Rig off and it's a normal navigation app for your car or pickup.
Where it falls short: it shows weigh stations on your route but not whether they're open, and there's no parking availability, no CarPlay yet and no load board. Big Rig is on iPhone now and comes to Android in the next update. It's $10 a month less than Trucker Path Diamond and $50 a year less on the annual plan.
More about FuelPilot Big Rig
### Hammer
Best for: drivers who want a truck GPS and don't want to pay for one.
Hammer is a free truck GPS from TruckersReport.com, with offline maps and lane guidance, covering the US, Canada and Mexico. If all you need is truck-safe directions, start here. You'll still be picking your own fuel stops.
### CoPilot Truck
Best for: drivers who run through areas with no signal and want navigation that works offline.
CoPilot is a long-running truck navigation app with offline maps. Truck navigation is a subscription, $9.99 a month or $119.99 a year in the US App Store, with a 14-day trial.
### Mudflap
Best for: cutting what you pay per gallon.
Mudflap isn't really a navigation app. It's a free app for discounted diesel at more than 3,600 truck stops, with savings that vary by stop and can reach $1.00 a gallon. There's no credit check, and paying by debit card or bank account has no fee. It also has free truck-safe navigation. Mudflap pairs well with a planning app: find out where you need to stop, then check whether a discounted stop is close.
### TruckMap
Best for: a free look at what's ahead.
TruckMap is a free truck GPS that shows diesel stations, weigh stations and parking. It's a good free backup to whatever you use as your main app.
### Sygic Truck & RV
Best for: drivers who want offline truck navigation, including outside North America.
Sygic is a truck and RV GPS with offline maps and routing for your vehicle's size. Truck navigation is a paid subscription; check the App Store for current prices. Like CoPilot and Hammer, it gets you there safely but leaves picking fuel stops to you.
### How to choose
- Parking is your biggest problem: stay with Trucker Path. Parking availability and its driver community are what it does best.
- Fuel is your biggest cost: use an app that plans stops from your range, like FuelPilot Big Rig or Trucker Path Diamond, and add Mudflap for discounts.
- You don't want to pay: Hammer for directions, Mudflap for discounts, TruckMap for stops and parking.
- You also drive a car or pull an RV: FuelPilot covers both in one app.
To see what fuel and fixed costs add up to per mile, try the free cost per mile calculator.
### Questions
#### What is the best alternative to Trucker Path?
It depends on what you use Trucker Path for. For fuel planning and IFTA miles at a lower price, FuelPilot Big Rig. For a free truck GPS, Hammer or TruckMap. For offline navigation, CoPilot Truck or Sygic Truck & RV. For diesel discounts, Mudflap. For parking, Trucker Path is still the one to beat.
#### Does Trucker Path plan fuel stops?
Yes, with a Diamond membership. Smart Fuel Plans use your truck's fuel settings and prices along your route to pick stops and how much fuel to add at each one.
#### Is there a cheaper truck GPS that plans fuel stops?
FuelPilot Big Rig is $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial. It plans truck-legal routes for your rig's size and picks the cheapest truck stops and truck lanes you can reach along the way.
#### Is there a free truck GPS app?
Yes. Hammer and TruckMap are free truck GPS apps, and Mudflap includes free truck-safe navigation alongside its diesel discounts.
#### Which truck app works for hot shots?
Any truck GPS that lets you enter your rig's height, weight and length. FuelPilot Big Rig has a Hot shot / HD pickup vehicle type, sends you to truck stops and truck lanes and plans from your real MPG.

## Blog (https://fuelpilotapp.com/blog/fuelpilot-vs-gasbuddy/)

### FuelPilot vs GasBuddy: a price map or a planned route?
November 25, 2026 · By David Kulagin, maker of FuelPilot
GasBuddy tells you what fuel costs near you and saves you money at the pump with its payment card. FuelPilot is turn-by-turn navigation that plans your fuel stops for the whole trip from your tank and your real MPG. For cheap gas around town, GasBuddy is hard to beat. For long trips, towing and diesel, FuelPilot does the planning GasBuddy leaves to you.
I make FuelPilot, so weigh this with that in mind. I've tried to be straight about where GasBuddy is the better app.
### The short version
- GasBuddy | FuelPilot
- What it is | Fuel price app with a payment card | Navigation app that plans fuel stops
- Where prices come from | Reported by its users | HERE Technologies
- Turn-by-turn directions | Gets you directions to a station | Built in, with spoken directions
- Picks your stops for a trip | You pick from prices along the route | Autopilot picks them from your range (Pro)
- Knows your towing range | No | Towing mode (Pro)
- Discount at the pump | Pay with GasBuddy card | None of its own; plans on the discounts you enter
- Trip and mileage log | Fuel log | Every navigated trip, with mileage and IFTA exports (Pro)
- Truck routing | No | Big Rig plan
- Price | Free; Plus $7.99/mo or $89/yr; Premium $9.99/mo or $99/yr | Free; Pro $7.99/mo or $49.99/yr; Big Rig $19.99/mo or $199.99/yr
Prices are US prices as listed in November 2026. Check each app before you buy.
### What GasBuddy does well
- Price coverage. GasBuddy's users report prices as they fill up, so in most towns you can see what every station is charging right now.
- Money off at the pump. Pay with GasBuddy is a payment card that takes money off each gallon. The paid Plus and Premium plans save 20¢ a gallon on your first 50 gallons each month, and Premium adds roadside assistance.
- Free tools. The app is free to use, with a trip cost calculator, a fuel log, fuel outage tracking and vehicle recall alerts.
- Route search. You can see prices along a route and choose where to stop.
If you mostly drive around town and want the cheapest gas nearby, GasBuddy does that job well and for free.
### What FuelPilot does differently
A price map tells you where fuel is cheap. It doesn't know how far your tank will get you, so you still have to work out which of those stations you can reach, then switch to a maps app to get there. On a long trip, or with a trailer behind you, that's where people run low or overpay at the only station left.
- It plans from your range. FuelPilot knows your tank size, learns your real MPG from your fill-ups and works out how far you can go.
- Autopilot picks the stops. Before you leave, it picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the whole trip, keeping the reserve you choose, and adds them to your directions. After each fill-up it checks that the next stop still makes sense.
- Towing mode. Turn it on when you hitch up and your range is planned for the trailer.
- It's the navigation app. Turn-by-turn directions with spoken guidance are built in, so you don't switch apps.
- Trips log themselves. Every drive you navigate is saved with its miles, time and fuel. With Pro you can export a mileage log, a fuel expense report or a quarterly IFTA summary.
- Trucks and RVs. The Big Rig plan routes for your rig's height, weight and length and sends semis and hot shots to truck stops and truck lanes only.
### Where GasBuddy is the better pick
- You drive locally and just want the cheapest gas near you.
- You want a discount card at the pump. FuelPilot doesn't have one.
- You want crowd-reported prices. FuelPilot's prices come from HERE and can lag behind the pump, so the price on the pump is the one you pay.
- You don't want to pay anything. FuelPilot's free plan has navigation and the cheapest gas near you, but Autopilot needs Pro.
### Where FuelPilot is the better pick
- Road trips and long runs where the stop you choose depends on how far your tank goes.
- Towing a travel trailer, fifth wheel or cargo trailer, when your range drops and you need stations you can actually reach.
- Diesel pickups, hot shots, semis and RVs that need truck-legal routes or truck lanes.
- Driving for work, when you need a mileage log or fuel expense report at tax time.
### Can you use both?
Yes. If you pay with a discount card, enter the discount once in FuelPilot under Settings › My discounts and it compares stations on the price you actually pay. Plenty of drivers keep GasBuddy for local fill-ups and plan road trips in FuelPilot.
Want to see what a trip will cost first? Try the free trip fuel cost calculator.
### Questions
#### Is FuelPilot better than GasBuddy?
They do different jobs. GasBuddy is better for finding cheap gas around town and for its pump discount card. FuelPilot is better for trips: it's a navigation app that picks the cheapest fuel stops you can reach from your tank and real MPG and adds them to your route.
#### Does GasBuddy plan fuel stops for a road trip?
GasBuddy shows prices along a route so you can choose where to stop. FuelPilot's Autopilot picks the stops for you from your range and reserve and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions.
#### Is FuelPilot free like GasBuddy?
FuelPilot is free to download and use for navigation and the cheapest gas near you, and a free account shows fuel prices along your route. Autopilot, towing mode and exports come with FuelPilot Pro, $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial.
#### Where do FuelPilot's fuel prices come from?
From HERE Technologies. GasBuddy's prices are reported by its users. Any app's prices can lag behind the pump, so the price on the pump is the one you pay.
#### Do both apps work in Canada?
Yes. Both work in the United States and Canada.
David Kulagin is a diesel mechanic who hauls for work. He founded Ghost Systems LLC, which makes FuelPilot.

## Free calculator (https://fuelpilotapp.com/tools/hot-shot-cost-per-mile-calculator/)

### Hot shot cost per mile calculator
Work out what every mile really costs your hot shot or owner-operator truck: fuel, maintenance and tires, your monthly payments and insurance, and the empty miles you don't get paid for. You'll get your cost per mile, cost per loaded mile and the rate you need just to break even.
### How it's worked out
- Miles per month = miles per week × 52 ÷ 12
- Fuel per mile = diesel price ÷ MPG
- Monthly costs per mile = monthly costs ÷ miles per month
- Total cost per mile = fuel + maintenance and tires + monthly costs per mile
- Break-even rate per loaded mile = total cost per mile ÷ (1 − empty miles ÷ 100)
The last step matters most. You pay for every mile, but you're only paid for the loaded ones. With 15% of your miles empty, every loaded mile has to cover about 1.18 miles of cost.
Example, using the numbers filled in above with diesel at $5.94: fuel is about 59¢ a mile, running costs about 74¢, and $2,500 a month in fixed costs over about 10,833 miles adds about 23¢. That's about 97¢ for every mile driven, or about $1.15 per loaded mile just to break even, before you pay yourself.
### What's not included
- Taxes. Income and self-employment tax, and any fuel tax you settle through IFTA, depend on your situation.
- Tolls, scales and lumpers. Add a monthly average under Everything else.
- Dispatch or factoring fees. If you pay a percentage, your rate has to cover that on top.
### Cut the biggest number: fuel
Fuel is often the biggest cost per mile. FuelPilot Big Rig picks the cheapest truck stop or truck lane you can reach for every stop on the run, on truck-legal routes for your rig's height, weight and length, and logs your miles by state for IFTA. There's a Hot shot / HD pickup vehicle type. Big Rig is $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year with a 7-day free trial, on iPhone now and on Android in the next update. More about Big Rig.
### Questions
#### How do I calculate cost per mile for a hot shot truck?
Add up your fuel per mile (diesel price ÷ MPG), maintenance and tires per mile, and your monthly fixed costs divided by the miles you drive in a month. Then divide by the share of miles that are loaded to get the rate you need per loaded mile.
#### What's a good cost per mile for hot shot trucking?
There isn't one number. It depends on your truck, your payments, insurance, MPG and how many miles you run. Running more miles spreads your fixed costs thinner, so the same truck costs less per mile the more it runs. Work out your own with the calculator and keep it current as fuel prices change.
#### How do empty miles affect my rate?
You pay for empty miles but aren't paid for them, so their cost has to come out of your loaded miles. Divide your cost per mile by the share of miles that are loaded. At 15% empty, multiply by about 1.18.
#### Does it work for a semi?
Yes. The math is the same for any truck. Put in your own MPG, miles and monthly costs.

## Free calculator (https://fuelpilotapp.com/tools/towing-range-calculator/)

### Towing range calculator
How far can you tow on a tank? Enter your tank size and MPG, and either your towing MPG or how much towing cuts it. You'll get your range on a full tank, how far to plan between fuel stops with a reserve left, and how much range the trailer costs you.
### How it's worked out
- Towing MPG = your towing MPG, or MPG × (1 − drop ÷ 100)
- Full-tank range = usable tank × towing MPG
- Miles between stops = full-tank range × (1 − reserve ÷ 100)
Example: a 36-gallon tank at 9 MPG towing is 324 miles on a full tank. Keep a quarter tank in reserve and you've got about 243 miles between stops.
### What drop to use
When Oak Ridge National Laboratory tested an SUV towing a 3,500 lb enclosed cargo trailer for the Department of Energy, fuel economy fell by about 30% in city driving and about 50% at 80 mph. Heavier, taller trailers, hills, headwinds and higher speeds push it toward the top of that range. The 35% starting value is a middle guess. Your own fill-ups are the only real answer: divide miles towed by gallons to refill, over two or three tanks, and put that in the towing MPG box.
For tank size, use the gallons it takes to fill up from empty, not a guess. Fuel gauges aren't exact, which is one more reason to keep a reserve.
### Plan stops around your real range
FuelPilot's towing mode adjusts your range for the trailer and learns your real MPG from your fill-ups. Autopilot then picks the cheapest stations you can reach for the whole trip, keeping the reserve you choose, and adds them to your turn-by-turn directions. Read the full guide: how to plan fuel stops when towing.
### Questions
#### How far can I tow on a tank of gas or diesel?
Multiply your usable tank size by your towing MPG. A 36-gallon tank at 9 MPG gives 324 miles on a full tank. Keeping a quarter tank in reserve leaves about 243 miles between stops.
#### How much does towing reduce range?
About as much as it reduces MPG. In a Department of Energy test, an SUV towing a 3,500 lb enclosed trailer lost about 30% of its fuel economy in city driving and about 50% at 80 mph. Heavy travel trailers and fifth wheels often fall somewhere in that range, depending on speed, wind and hills.
#### How much reserve should I keep when towing?
A quarter tank is a common rule. Keep more in remote areas, in winter, or before a long climb.
#### Why is my towing range lower than the calculator says?
Headwinds, hills, speed and idling all cut MPG, and fuel gauges aren't exact. Measure your towing MPG over a few tanks and use that.

## Free calculator (https://fuelpilotapp.com/tools/trip-fuel-cost-calculator/)

### Trip fuel cost calculator
Enter how far you're going, your MPG and the price of fuel to see what the trip will cost, how many gallons you'll burn and the cost per mile. Works for gas or diesel, one way or round trip, and splits the cost if you're sharing the ride.
### How it's worked out
- Gallons = miles ÷ MPG
- Fuel cost = gallons × price per gallon
- Cost per mile = price per gallon ÷ MPG
Example: a 500-mile drive at 22 MPG uses about 22.7 gallons. At $4.00 a gallon that's about $90.91, or about 18¢ a mile. Round trip, double it.
### Getting a closer number
- Use your real MPG, not the sticker. Divide the miles you drove by the gallons it took to fill back up, over a couple of tanks.
- Highway speed matters. Fuel economy usually drops quickly above about 50 mph, so a fast highway trip can come in under your average MPG.
- Towing changes everything. A trailer can cut your MPG by a third or more. Use the towing range calculator to plan stops.
- Prices vary along the way. The same trip can cost noticeably more or less depending on where you stop.
### Let FuelPilot pick the cheap stops
This calculator tells you what a trip costs at one price. FuelPilot checks prices along your actual route, picks the cheapest stations you can reach with your tank and real MPG, and gives you turn-by-turn directions to each one. Navigation is free; Autopilot fuel stops come with FuelPilot Pro.
### Questions
#### How do I calculate the fuel cost of a road trip?
Divide the miles by your MPG to get gallons, then multiply by the price per gallon. A 500-mile trip at 22 MPG and $4.00 a gallon is about 22.7 gallons, or about $90.91.
#### How do I work out fuel cost per mile?
Divide the price per gallon by your MPG. At $4.00 a gallon and 22 MPG, fuel costs about 18¢ a mile. At $5.94 diesel and 10 MPG, it's about 59¢ a mile.
#### Is the calculator accurate for diesel?
Yes. The math is the same for any fuel. Pick Diesel to start from the national average diesel price, then change it to the price you expect to pay.
#### Does it work in Canada?
The calculator uses miles and US gallons. For litres and kilometres, convert first: 1 US gallon is 3.785 litres and 1 mile is 1.609 km.
